notes: Test cases for the house-style skill. The mechanical assertions are graded by scripts/grade.mjs, which reuses check-prose.mjs so the grader and the skill can never disagree about what a violation is. The judgment assertions are graded by reading the output.

evals.name: draft-from-notes
evals.prompt: I've got raw notes at <inputs>/queue-backlog-notes.md about a queue backlog incident on my sim racing platform. Write me the opening and the Context section for a case study on it, the same as the ones at /work.
evals.expected_output: An opening that starts on a concrete fact or number from the notes rather than a thesis, and a Context section, in the practitioner-teacher voice. Zero em dashes, zero contractions, American spelling, no disallow-list words, one line per paragraph.

assertions.text: Draft contains no em dashes in body prose
Draft contains no contractions
Draft uses American spelling throughout
Draft avoids the disallow-list words seam and load-bearing
Every prose paragraph occupies a single line (no hard wrapping)
Draft includes a Context section heading
Opening leads with a concrete fact, number or scene rather than a thesis statement
Uses real figures from the notes (47 sessions, 11 days, 6 drivers, 99.4%) and invents none

evals.name: audit-before-publish
evals.prompt: Can you review <inputs>/rate-limiting-draft.mdx before I publish it? I want to know what needs fixing.
evals.expected_output: A review naming the planted mechanical violations (3 em dashes, 7 contractions, 3 British spellings, seam and load-bearing, 5 wrapped paragraphs) plus the voice problems, without modifying the input file.

assertions.text: Review flags the em dashes
Review flags the contractions
Review flags the British spellings (organisation, optimised, behaviour)
Review flags both disallow-list words as violations, not merely quoting the lines they appear on
Review does not itself use a disallow-list word in its own prose
Review flags the hard line wrapping
The input draft file was left unmodified by the audit
The review prose itself contains no em dashes
Review identifies at least one voice problem beyond mechanics (empty adjectives, hedging, passionate about, thesis-first opening)

evals.name: tighten-a-paragraph
evals.prompt: Tighten this paragraph for me, it's going in the caching post: [a marketing-register paragraph containing 2 em dashes, 4 contractions, British 'optimisations', stacked empty adjectives, a hedge, and the empty claim 'the results speak for themselves']
evals.expected_output: A rewritten paragraph in voice: no em dashes, no contractions, American spelling, empty adjectives replaced by mechanism, hedge and empty claim removed. Numbers are absent from the source, so the response should ask for them or mark their absence rather than invent them.

assertions.text: Rewrite contains no em dashes
Rewrite contains no contractions
Rewrite uses American spelling (optimizations, not optimisations)
Rewritten paragraph is on a single line
The hedge 'it could be argued' is gone
The empty claim 'the results speak for themselves' is gone
Does not invent latency figures or percentages that were not in the source; asks for real numbers or marks the gap instead
Replaces the empty adjectives (game-changer, sophisticated, intelligent, robust) with mechanism or removes them
